Simulate Interest Rate Paths for OAS Analysis

Source: R/rate-modeling.r
simulate_rates.Rd

Interfaces with the dnsr package to simulate interest rate paths for use in option-adjusted spread analysis.

Usage

simulate_rates(
  dns_params,
  n_paths = 100,
  n_periods = 360,
  maturities = c(0.25, 0.5, 1, 2, 3, 5, 7, 10, 20, 30),
  frequency = "monthly",
  seed = NULL,
  engine = c("yuima", "exact"),
  include_t0 = TRUE
)

Arguments

dns_params

List. Model parameters from dnsr package, typically from dnsr::get_calibrated_dns_params(). Its lambda element is the Nelson-Siegel decay rate, in the same units as maturities – that is, per year. Diebold and Li's conventional 0.0609 is per month, so the equivalent here is 0.0609 * 12 = 0.7308. Passing the per-month value against a grid in years puts the curvature hump 29 years out, which leaves the slope and curvature loadings correlated -0.97 over a standard 3M-30Y grid; simulate_rates() warns when the loadings come out that close together. See dnsr::ns_lambda() to express a decay rate by the maturity at which the curvature loading peaks.

n_paths

Integer. Number of simulation paths

n_periods

Integer. Number of time periods (typically months)

maturities

Numeric vector. Maturities (in years) for which to calculate yields

frequency

Character. Time frequency, one of "monthly" (default), "quarterly", or "annual"

seed

Integer. Random seed for reproducibility

engine

Character. Simulation engine passed to dnsr::simulate_dns_factors(): "yuima" (the dnsr default, which needs the yuima package) or "exact", which samples the exact transition law and needs no extra package. Defaults to dnsr's own choice.

include_t0

Logical. dnsr returns the deterministic t = 0 curve followed by one column per simulated step, so the result has n_periods + 1 columns and column 1 is identical on every path. TRUE, the default, keeps it: path-consistent discounting needs it, because the rate prevailing over month 1 is the one observed at time 0. FALSE drops it, giving exactly n_periods columns with column t being month t. Either way the columns are named by their period, so the convention is visible in the object.

Value

A list containing:

yield_paths

A list of matrices, one for each maturity, with dimensions [path, time]

factors

The simulated DNS factors

params

The DNS parameters used for simulation

maturities

The maturities for which yields were calculated

Examples

if (FALSE) { # \dontrun{
dns_params <- dnsr::get_calibrated_dns_params()
rate_paths <- simulate_rates(dns_params, n_paths = 100, n_periods = 360,
                             maturities = c(0.25, 0.5, 1, 2, 3, 5, 7, 10, 20, 30))
} # }
